recipes.name: Avocado and Tuna Tapas
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 ounce) can solid white tuna packed in water, drained
3 green onions, thinly sliced, plus additional for garnish
1 pinch garlic salt, or to taste

steps.text: Stir together tuna, mayonnaise, green onions, red pepper, and balsamic vinegar in a bowl.
Season with pepper and garlic salt, then pack the avocado halves with the tuna mixture.
Garnish with reserved green onions and a dash of black pepper before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Avocado and Tuna Tapas
raw_recipe.description: Avocado halves are filled with a tangy tuna salad in this Spanish tapas style tuna stuffed avocado. This light, healthy dish goes best with crisp white wines and crunchy bread.

video.description: Drop the sandwich bread and give your tuna salad the royal healthy treatment by presenting in avocado cups. With a bit of red pepper for crunch, you’ll love how easy preparation is for this lunch, snack or light dinner.

review.reviewBody: I was hesitant to make this at first but I was hungry, had all the ingredients at hand and really didn't feel like eating fastfood. This is soo good. I even got an "mmm..mmm" from my hubby. Although I am not a big fan of canned tuna I do love avocados and keep finding ways to make it a part of my diet. Avocados are loaded with MUFA's (mono-unsaturated fat -->the good kind) which actually helps your body get rid of the "bad" fat. So Gracias for sharing this recipe!

This was a basic tuna salad recipe stuffed in an avocado. I really enjoy the idea of tuna salad in an avocado and it has inspired me to think outside the box. Next time I will try to put a Mexican spin on it by adding cumin, tomato and some chipotle to the dressing. The filing is a little dry as written; I did add an equal amount of plain yogurt to the mayonnaise for a little healthier version. This is a solid base off of which you can customize to your own tastes.

I added "Flavor bomb" snacking tomatoes, a sprinkle of dried dill, and adjusted ingredient amounts for a serving since I wanted to eat the whole avocado. Even after adjusting ingredients, this still clocks at under 500 calories. The mayo I used was chosen foods avocado mayo and the balsamic vinegar was a decent quality Balsamic Vinegar of Modena. It's a beautiful quick and healthy meal with great flavors.

I really liked this but did make some changes to brighten us up. I used another tablespoon of mayonnaise. Squeezed juice from 1/2 a lime. Then I added about 2-3 tablespoons on minced cilantro. Then mixed the filling together and garnished with some fresh cilantro leaves. I served it as a meal with corn on the Cobb and sliced fresh tomatoes. Everyone loved it! Yum.
Awesome recipe! I scraped out some of the avocado, made a small guac side, and used cherry tomatoes instead of the red bell pepper. Switched purple onions for the green onions...tasted great!
I've often used small shrimp in place of the tuna, and it's delicious! Simple easy meal with just a salad.

Delicious! I used white albacore packed in olive oil as my own preference and it turned out amazing!! I also scooped a little of the avocado out before packing it and mixed it into the tuna mixture so I could fit more tuna in each one... my family love them! Thank you for a great recipe I’ll be keeping around :)

We loved this for it's great flavor and think this is a wonderful summer time recipe. I actually poached a tuna steak the day before in olive oil using Chef John's Olive Oil Poached Tuna recipe, easy. I had read some of the comments about the recipe being a little dry, but didn't want to add any more mayo so I simply diced a seeded plum tomato and that was a nice add. Thank for this great recipe!

This is a great and easy dish to serve as a snack or appetizer. Tune the balsamic vinegar to suit your tastes. It's also good with some smoked paprika on top. Use a 5.5 oz can of tuna (or more avocado), because a 12 oz can is waaaaaay too much. I also found that the format of tuna on half avocados hard to eat. Instead I lay a bed of sliced avocado and spread the tuna on top.

Rated as written using low salt canned chicken breast, 1 tsp white balsamic vinegar and 2 Tbsp mayo. Vanished at a progressive dinner as the first course; at a tailgate party on baguettes with diced avocado garnish; and devoured by picky small fry in cherry tomatoes after school. (Also lends itself well to additions) Thanks for a great recipe!

This has become our Saturday 'go-to' lunch. Quick and easy. I usually double the filling as we love the flavours. I also drizzle some really good Kalamata olive oil over the top for an added burst. So delicious and healthy. I do use homemade mayo as it's so much better tasting than store bought.

Theres countless ways you can doctor this. More veggies different veggies, I also love smoked paprika sprinkled directly on the avocados before stuffing and s couple drops of Liquid Smoke and minced onion in my "salad" (works well with canned chicken and other kinds of canned fish, just find the flavor profile you like best. Its really quite fool proof)
A great lunch. I added little grape tomatoes from my garden.
Wow - had these for dinner and breakfast! Such a great combo, fresh and super satisfying.

This is good. I had one of those nights I didn’t want to cook and wanted something healthy. Simple, quick and delicious. I love the crunch the bell pepper adds. I did put grape tomatoes on top since others said they did that and did a side of tortilla chips. It was a perfect dinner!
I tried this recipe for the first time tonight. I added onion and tomato and a splash of coconut amino, in addition to the balsamic vinegar. Old bay seasoning, sea salt, and black pepper.
Very tasty! I wasn't sure what to expect but I was surprised at how good it is!
Quick, easy, and delicious! Full of flavor, as well as healthy fats and protein. This is my favorite tuna tapas recipe. So simple!
